purpose: Evaluation of candidate source-occurrence identity designs (task §7/§33). Design-only; no production code implements any of these yet.

options.name: Span-primary
options.determinism: Yes - parseDocumentStructure is a pure function of doc.text; no iteration-order dependency reaches charStart
options.uniqueness: Two nodes of the same type cannot legitimately share a charStart in one parse pass (overlapsAny already prevents accepting overlapping matches); cross-type collision at the same offset is exceptionally unlikely and is caught by explicit collision detection, never silently resolved
options.collisionRisk: Near-zero by construction; residual risk handled by fail-closed detection (I5/§28), not assumed away
options.stability: Level A only (same source bytes + same parser version) - deliberately does not promise stability across a parser algorithm change or re-extraction, which is the correct scope (cross-version stability is a lineage concern, not an occurrence-identity concern)
options.readability: Low (opaque hash) - mitigated by keeping sectionRef/heading/charStart as separate, always-present display fields
options.performance: O(1) per node, no extra text scan
options.migrationComplexity: Low - charStart is already computed and present on every StructuralNode
options.parserVersionSensitivity: Intentionally sensitive (a parser change should mint new identities, not silently keep stale ones)
options.extractionVersionSensitivity: Intentionally sensitive (re-extraction is a different source representation)
options.amendmentVersionBehavior: N/A by design - amendment/version lineage is explicitly a separate mechanism (§11 of the ADR)
options.downstreamErgonomics: Reuses the existing repo-wide computeStableKey convention (stable-keys.ts) - no new hashing scheme introduced
options.verdict: STRONG - selected as the identity mechanism within the preferred hybrid (Option D)

options.name: Ancestry path + occurrence ordinal
options.determinism: Fragile - depends on parent ids already being resolved, which is exactly the question under dispute when labels collide
options.uniqueness: Not self-contained - circular bootstrapping (a node's id depends on its parent's id, all the way to the root)
options.collisionRisk: Fragile to reordering: a future parser-version change to intra-region iteration order could silently shift occurrenceOrdinal for nodes that did not themselves move
options.stability: Worse than Option A - depends transitively on every ancestor's own identity stability
options.readability: High - intuitively debuggable, encodes hierarchy directly
options.performance: Requires a top-down pass; not O(1) per node in isolation
options.migrationComplexity: Higher - needs parent resolution order enforced
options.parserVersionSensitivity: High, and in an uncontrolled way (ordinal can shift without the node itself moving)
options.downstreamErgonomics: Good readability, but the bootstrapping/circularity problem disqualifies it as primary identity
options.verdict: REJECTED as primary identity mechanism - retained as a derived, non-identity structuralPath/occurrenceOrdinal display field computed from Option A ids (Option D)

options.name: Content-derived hash + source position
options.uniqueness: DISQUALIFYING FLAW: introduces NEW collisions rather than removing them - real drafting contains verbatim-repeated boilerplate opening language across genuinely distinct provisions (e.g. two different baskets both opening identical text in different sections)
options.collisionRisk: Higher than today's scheme for this specific failure mode
options.stability: Superficially attractive (survives whitespace-only re-extraction) but not worth the uniqueness cost
options.performance: Extra text scan + hash per node, for no benefit Option A doesn't already provide via charStart
options.extractionVersionSensitivity: Partially resistant, but at the cost of uniqueness (the actual goal)
options.downstreamErgonomics: Circular dependency: a node's 'own text' is only correctly knowable once children are occurrence-safely attributed, which is DOWNSTREAM of identity, not independent of it - this option needs the bug already fixed to compute its own input
options.verdict: REJECTED - introduces new collisions and has a circular dependency on the very defect being fixed

options.name: Hybrid: span-primary identity + path/ordinal disambiguation metadata (PREFERRED)
options.construction: nodeId identical to Option A's construction; structuralPath (sequence of ancestor nodeIds, computed top-down AFTER nodeIds exist) and occurrenceOrdinal (Option B's sibling-occurrence counter) carried as separate, non-identity, display/debug-only fields
options.determinism: Inherits Option A's determinism for the identity itself; structuralPath/occurrenceOrdinal are derived, never consulted for equality or lookup
options.uniqueness: Inherits Option A's uniqueness guarantee exactly - the metadata fields cannot cause a collision because they play no role in Map keys or lookups
options.collisionRisk: Same as Option A (near-zero, fail-closed on the residual)
options.stability: Same scope as Option A (Level A)
options.readability: High - gets Option A's safety AND Option B's human-legibility, without Option B's circularity, because the legible fields are strictly additive metadata
options.performance: Same as Option A plus one cheap top-down pass to compute display metadata (not on the hot path of any lookup)
options.migrationComplexity: Low-medium - same as A, plus one additional derived-field computation pass
options.amendmentVersionBehavior: Same as Option A - explicitly out of scope, handled by Phase 2G's own lineage mechanism
options.downstreamErgonomics: Best of both: safe map-key identity + legible debug/display fields
options.verdict: SELECTED - matches the task's own §7D framing ('hybrid deterministic identity: span-primary with path-ordinal disambiguation') exactly

options.name: Corroborating prior art (not itself a candidate mechanism)
options.construction: N/A - not a construction formula, a reference precedent: Prisma DocumentNode.parentId (real DB-generated FK, @@unique([companyId, stableKey]))
options.note: Confirms the general direction (occurrence-safe identity, parent/child by identity not label) already works correctly one layer over in this same codebase for the legacy/solver-native persistence model. Not adoptable directly for the in-memory index (task explicitly excludes DB-autoincrement dependence for that layer, and a DB round-trip has no place in a pure in-memory parse step) - cited as evidence supporting Option D's direction, not as an alternative construction.

rejectedAlternativesSummary.optionC: introduces new collisions from repeated boilerplate text + circular dependency on the defect being fixed
rejectedAlternativesSummary.secondIndependentParser: evaluated separately (ADR §19) - cost/complexity/disagreement-resolution problems outweigh marginal independence gain over the cheaper mechanical reachability-invariant approach
